title: pvWavelet
body:
## pvWavelet

Generates image data over WholeExtent (spacing SubsampleRate, origin 0) with the point scalar "RTData" = Maximum·exp(-r²/(2·StandardDeviation²)) + XMag·sin(XFreq·x) + YMag·sin(YFreq·y) + ZMag·cos(ZFreq·z), where x, y, z are offsets from Center divided by the extent width on each axis and r is their length. It is ParaView's standard synthetic volume, used to test contouring, slicing, volume rendering and exports. The curated wavelet operation offers Schemaxis defaults.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- The native documentation writes the terms as a product; VTK adds them, so the Gaussian and the waves superpose.
- Center is in index coordinates, not physical units, because spacing is 1 (or SubsampleRate).
- Schemaxis generates this source from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for it, so inspect the output before relying on it.

Native constructor: `Wavelet`. Identity: `sources/RTAnalyticSource`. Role: `pipeline`. Output kinds: `["data"]`.

### Inputs

No connected inputs (source/resource).


### Options

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Center` | Centre of the Gaussian and origin of the wave coordinates, in grid-index units: for each point, x, y and z are the offsets of its grid index from Center, divided by the extent width on that axis, and the Gaussian depends on their length r. It is not in physical units. ParaView's own text refers to "the equation" it prints, which multiplies the terms; the filter adds them to the Gaussian. | `{"items":{"type":"number"},"maxItems":3,"minItems":3,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `[1,1,1]` |
| `Maximum` | This parameter specifies the maximum value (M) of the function. | `{"type":"number"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1` |
| `StandardDeviation` | This property specifies the standard deviation of the Gaussian used in computing this function. | `{"type":"number"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1` |
| `SubsampleRate` | This property specifies the rate at which to subsample the volume. The extent of the dataset in each dimension will be divided by this value. (See the Whole Extent property.) | `{"minimum":1,"type":"integer"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1` |
| `WholeExtent` | The six values in this property indicate the X, Y, and Z extent of the output data. The first two values represent the minimum and maximum X indices, the next two are the minimum and maximum Y indices, and the last two are the minimum and maximum Z indices. | `{"items":{"type":"integer"},"maxItems":6,"minItems":6,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `[1,1,1,1,1,1]` |
| `XFreq` | Natural frequency of the x wave, the XFreq in XMag·sin(XFreq·x); x is the offset from Center divided by the extent width in x. ParaView's own text refers to "the equation" it prints, which multiplies the terms; the filter adds them to the Gaussian. | `{"type":"number"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1` |
| `XMag` | Amplitude of the x wave: the term XMag·sin(XFreq·x) that is added to RTData. ParaView's own text refers to "the equation" it prints, which multiplies the terms; the filter adds them to the Gaussian. | `{"type":"number"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1` |
| `YFreq` | Natural frequency of the y wave, the YFreq in YMag·sin(YFreq·y); y is the offset from Center divided by the extent width in y. ParaView's own text refers to "the equation" it prints, which multiplies the terms; the filter adds them to the Gaussian. | `{"type":"number"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1` |
| `YMag` | Amplitude of the y wave: the term YMag·sin(YFreq·y) that is added to RTData. ParaView's own text refers to "the equation" it prints, which multiplies the terms; the filter adds them to the Gaussian. | `{"type":"number"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1` |
| `ZFreq` | Natural frequency of the z wave, the ZFreq in ZMag·cos(ZFreq·z); z is the offset from Center divided by the extent width in z. ParaView's own text refers to "the equation" it prints, which multiplies the terms; the filter adds them to the Gaussian. | `{"type":"number"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1` |
| `ZMag` | Amplitude of the z wave: the term ZMag·cos(ZFreq·z) that is added to RTData. ParaView's own text refers to "the equation" it prints, which multiplies the terms; the filter adds them to the Gaussian. | `{"type":"number"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1` |

```json
  "id": "result",
  "filter": "pvWavelet"
}
```
